basis: Deficiency of mucosal secretory IgA transport defines an immunodeficiency; intestinal symptoms and candidiasis lack frequencies establishing common direct gut damage.
Mature B-cell lymphoma primarily involving lymph nodes; marrow, hepatic and gastrointestinal involvement is explicitly infrequent.
Severe neonatal dilated cardiomyopathy; associated pulmonary arterial hypertension affects the cardiovascular axis.
Axonal peripheral neuropathy; muscle wasting in 7-8/8 and fixed foot deformities in 4-6/6 support musculoskeletal involvement. Diabetes is a separate disease.
Intellectual disability, cardiac anomalies and joint/skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; coloboma occurs in 30-79%. Hearing impairment (30-79%) omitted because of the cap.
Immune-mediated glomerular inflammation following streptococcal infection; acute hypertension and edema do not establish separate cardiovascular damage.
Congenital defect of the muscular diaphragm; associated pulmonary hypoplasia commonly impairs lung development and function in well over 30% of clinically affected patients.
Defined by sweat-gland dysfunction, sparse or brittle hair, and missing teeth; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Immune-mediated lymphoepithelial infiltration of salivary glands; associated HIV, Sjogren syndrome and later lymphoma do not establish additional organ involvement.
Adenoma arising in the parathyroid gland; neither hormone excess nor common skeletal damage is established for this histologic subtype.
Familial temporal lobe epilepsy defined by focal seizures and temporal auras; no extracerebral organ damage is established.
Mycobacterial infection warrants the infectious mechanism axis; the affected reproductive organs have no anatomical axis.
Umbrella of single-protein peroxisomal metabolic defects; neurologic, hepatic, renal and skeletal damage varies by subtype and is not established across most patients.
Small cell carcinoma of pulmonary origin, detectable only by sputum cytology; no additional organ occupation is established.
Pulmonary and pleural LAM; renal angiomyolipomas occur in ~30-50% and are a major diagnostic feature. Ungual fibromas reflect associated tuberous sclerosis.
The concept and ancestors establish severe skeletal dysplasia; common marrow or pancreatic involvement cannot be inferred from the SBDS name alone.
The definition establishes a parathyroid gland adenoma despite the nonspecific name and parent; no additional organ damage is established.
Inherited platelet deficiency; additional organ involvement belongs to particular syndromic subtypes rather than most patients across this umbrella.
Premature fusion of a single squamosal cranial suture is a skull disorder; common neurologic injury is not established.
Developmental disability and hypotonia in 5/5, with callosal abnormalities; short stature and minor digit dysmorphism do not establish damaging musculoskeletal disease.
Glycine metabolism defect with severe neonatal encephalopathy and developmental impairment; central apnea does not establish direct pulmonary damage.
Abnormally elevated blood glucose is a metabolic disturbance; blood glucose elevation itself is not a blood-cell disorder or evidence of other organ damage.
Interstitial 12q deletion syndromes commonly cause developmental delay or intellectual disability; other organ defects vary with the deleted interval and lack commonality evidence.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss in 6/6; WHRN-related syndromic retinal disease is outside this concept.
Congenital obstruction or atresia of the lacrimal drainage system; sinusitis and inflammatory complications are occasional and do not support additional axes.
